stacked_on: SV2-PRF-01 branch engineer-323133-1099, pull request open when this package was built
status: measured on Anton by read only reads and on a CI runner by a kind fixture with an interrupted registry
evidence_class: Measured: two read only Anton reads (kubectl get nodes, events and Pods; aws describe scaling activities and instances) at 2026-10-11T14:57:15Z and 15:59:13Z, each covering the hour of events Kubernetes keeps; three Startup stages runs (38150051995, 38150380291, 38153743721) on GitHub hosted runners pulled the published worker image through a local registry, the later two behind a 90 second outage on both kind workers. Attribution, report, claim and the account release are functions over committed reads; the account release runs the KUB-05 recovery over fakeredis and is mocked. No antoncore object, autoscaler setting or deployed Pod was changed.
interfaces: scripts.swarm_v2.startup_stages.reduce(raw) keeps only the event reasons, node Ready transitions, Pod creation and readiness, and successful ASG launch activities joined to EC2 launch times that attribution reads

startup_stages.attribute(read) gives one sample per Pod with scheduling or failure evidence: node kind (cold when an instance requested after the Pod waited served it), node source (existing, new_instance, warm_pool), from_zero from the scale up that requested that instance, image cache (cached, uncached, partial, unknown), outcome (started, pending or a failure class), transient failure the Pod started past, sandbox retries, time to first failure and stages trigger, instance, join, schedule, image, pod_start, bootstrap; a Pod listed after its scheduling event is a later incarnation and its listing is ignored

startup_stages.report(samples) gives startup_stage_p50_p95 per scenario with failures, pending and transient counts beside the starts, node_provision_ms (trigger plus instance plus join) apart from image_init_ms (pull plus Pod start)
startup_stages.claim(samples, cold_scale_from_zero) raises ClaimRefused naming every sample that landed on an existing node, came from a non empty pool or did not pull uncached
startup_stages.unbounded(samples, grace) lists pull failures, final or transient, classified later than the KUB-05 pull grace or never timed
python -m scripts.swarm_v2.startup_bench reduce, report and claim expose those on the command line; claim exits 2 with the refusal and writes nothing

tests/performance/swarm_v2/startup.py drives the kind fixture: uncached then cached worker image on each node, then every node pulling while the local registry is stopped for --outage seconds, recovery waited, capture written for reduce
.github/workflows/startup-stages.yml runs the fixture on dispatch, on call and on branch pushes touching the fixture or the startup modules, and uploads the startup-stages artifact

supported_versions.cluster: Anton k3s v1.33.12 with containerd 2.2.3 and the installed cluster autoscaler; kind v0.33.0 with node image v1.37.0 in CI
supported_versions.compatibility: New modules and a new workflow only; the local runtime and every deployed object are unchanged. The worker resources workflow now triggers only on its own workloads folder.

authority: The benchmark only reads. Anton reads used read only kubectl and aws describe calls; the kind fixture creates and deletes objects only inside its own throwaway cluster and namespace. A cold label is granted only by claim over the samples' own provenance, never by a scenario name or a caller label.
authoritative_objects: None are written. Raw listings stay outside the repository; only reduced reads with the sha256 of every listing are committed. The fixture deletes only its own namespace in its own kind cluster.

findings: Ondemand new instances join in 36 to 37 s after EC2 launch, warm pool instances in 22 s, the swarm pool c7i-flex instances in 46 and 56 s.

On the swarm pool the Pod waited a further 75 and 96 s after the node turned Ready: the scheduler reported the Pod's node affinity or selector unmatched on the new node for that time. A node label applied after join is the likely cause; it is a hypothesis, filed as a ledger follow up.
Every ondemand cold start in read 1 hit one FailedCreatePodSandBox retry, and its Pod start ran 30 to 70 s beyond the pull.
A pull blocked by a 90 s registry outage started 90 to 175 s after scheduling, up to 85 s after the registry returned, because kubelet pull back off keeps growing during the outage.

limitations: Bootstrap ends at the worker image's own report in the kind fixture; the native harness handshake needs a controller grant and provider credentials and is not measured.
Anton samples are the workloads that ran in each hour, mostly CI runners and services, not swarm workers; only two swarm pool scale from zero samples exist.
Events older than an hour are gone, so each read only sees the hour before it.
EC2 launch times have one second precision.
The kind registry runs on the same runner, so its pull times reflect image size and unpack, not registry distance.
With two cold samples in read 2 the p95 equals the maximum.
rollback: Use the previous qualified image and reduce launch concurrency: this package changes no deployed image, concurrency or autoscaler setting, so rollback is reverting its pull request; the measurement workflow is removed with it. Rehearsed in the fixture: the registry outage left both Pods recovering to start without a manual step, and the recovery case shows the account slot released past the pull grace with nothing left reserved.
